Many times, those with power and influence are the recipients of many of the resources and when available to them, they will strive to get more for their own sake and benefit. Many of the most vulnerable residents lack this power and influence to benefit from many of the resources in our city. Knowing this, as an elected leader I will always fight for all members of our community, especially paying attention to our most vulnerable residents. I plan to invite and encourage more participation from all members of our community by doing more outreach and being a source of relatability and reliance. I will make it easier for our community members to access county budgets, revenue and expenses, and different investments that we make in our city. I am sure there are inactive residents that, given an opportunity to be involved, would help voice their wants and ideas to better spend our tax dollars and help the government be more impactful towards our population and long-term goals in the community.

Meet with the Housing Developers that have developed housing in the last 8 years and ask them what Government can do, whether it be changing regulations and requirements to have more affordable housing. If a solution cannot be found with our private sector or private-public partnerships, then our government will have to take a much more aggressive and active role in finding the solution by looking at what has been done in other parts of the county, state, country, and other countries. I appreciate the work of Pittsburg's law enforcement officers who serve and protect our community every day. I support continuing to build strong relationships and trust between our police officers and the residents they serve. We can strengthen public safety by providing officers with quality training, modern equipment and technology, effective body cameras, and the resources they need to do their jobs safely and professionally. I also believe accountability and transparency are essential to maintaining the public's trust. When misconduct occurs, it should be addressed fairly, thoroughly, and according to the law. By supporting both our officers and strong standards of accountability, we can continue building a safer Pittsburg for everyone.

#### Homelessness/Unhoused

I believe most of the cases of homelessness have stemmed from either a drug addiction or psychiatric disability, psychiatric illness, emotional disorders, or mental disabilities. There are some homeless shelters that provide warm shelter and food. However, rightfully so many, if not all, homeless shelters have basic rules such as no drugs and seek to limit what homeless people can bring to the shelter. This might cause a homeless person to find shelter elsewhere to be able to keep their items or pursue their drug habits without someone dictating their actions. Like rebels, some homeless people maintain a sense of wanting to live free and survive on their own terms. There are also people with economic reasons that have resulted in homelessness, especially with the ever-increasing cost of housing and the required pre-requisite of having good credit to qualify for most rentals.
To reduce homelessness in our city our designated County and City government leaders and team members from both Government and non-profit organizations must work together to establish a comprehensive data base or our homeless population that is updated and kept up to date. We will learn if individual homeless people are a young person, a member of a family, a single adult, a veteran, or a chronic homeless person. Once we have comprehensive information, we will build teams of people from across our government and non-profit organizations, including volunteers, that want to make a difference. Every homeless person has unique needs, and we will have to address them one by one, making progress with the goal of helping everyone find and achieve sustainable warm shelter and food.
The goal would be to have them integrated once again into our community, by becoming independent, feeling good about themselves, and becoming the next great teachers and volunteers to those that, like them, were once in need.
